No — it needs changes before publishing. Two problems:

**1. "Fully compliant with the framework" — overstated-lineage claim.**
NIST SP 800-61 is a legitimate public source, so citing it is fine, but "fully compliant" is a formal compliance/certification claim, not an influence claim. Unless you've actually undergone (or can point to) a real compliance assessment, this is exactly the kind of assurance-sounding language that creates risk for regulated or enterprise customers who may rely on it. Reword to influence language, e.g.:

> "Our workflow is informed by / draws on the incident-handling structure in NIST SP 800-61."

**2. The uncited conference talk — unverified source.**
An unlinked, unverifiable talk shouldn't be presented as a citable source of lineage in public docs — a hostile or careful reader (or a customer's compliance team) can't verify it. Either:
- Find and link the actual talk/speaker, and add it to your source map as `verified-public`, or
- Drop the specific claim and generalize it (e.g., "general SRE incident-response practices") so you're not implying a real citation exists, or
- Mark it internally as "public URL needed" and leave it out of the public doc until resolved.

**Suggested rewrite:**

> "Our workflow draws on the incident-handling structure described in NIST SP 800-61, along with general SRE incident-response practices."

This keeps honest lineage (real source, framed as influence) without any compliance claim or unverifiable citation. Want me to also check/update `source-map.md` and `source-to-concept-crosswalk.md` for these two references?
